_derivation.note: SELF-DECLARED CONTRACT — Google Sheets is a user-defined tabular source. There is no provider field catalog to exhaustively enumerate: the Sheets API returns whatever columns the user has placed in their spreadsheet. The canonical fields declared in official_fields.json are the toorow tabular-objectives contract v1, defined by the product (not by Google). The transport (GET spreadsheets.values endpoint) is documented at the URL below; the field contract is toorow-defined.
_derivation.contract_rationale: Fields represent the three KPI objectives (budget_declared, target_revenue, target_conversions) plus the two structural dimensions (date, sheet_row_id) that every toorow-connected sheet must expose via its datastream column_mapping. This is a closed, minimal contract by design: users declare their own column names; the mapping translates them to these canonical names at pull time.

sources._note: This URL documents the Sheets API v4 transport (spreadsheets.values.get / batchGet). It is NOT a field catalog — the field contract is toorow-defined (see official_fields.json and the _derivation note above). The response shape is: { 'values': [[header_row], [data_row], ...] }. Field names are user-defined column headers resolved at runtime via the datastream column_mapping.

probe.structural_note: Tabular contract: columns are declared by the user-mapped sheet, not enumerable via a provider field API. ratify_connector.py records a structural ratification (catalog==contract by construction) rather than issuing a field-by-field probe.

_exposure_note: Self-declared tabular contract: the 5 fields are the extraction contract by construction.
